name: Storage & Warehousing
short: Short- and long-term household storage in sealed, inventoried units — between leases, renovations or postings.
description: When dates don't line up — a lease gap, a renovation, a posting abroad — your home can wait safely. Goods are packed to move standard, inventoried box by box, sealed and stored, then re-delivered when you're ready. Storage charges are stated per month per volume before anything enters the unit.

features.title: Packed to move standard, then sealed
features.text: Storage goods get the same packing discipline as a move — so re-delivery is a simple, safe operation months later.

features.title: Box-level inventory
features.text: Every carton and item is listed before storage; partial retrievals are possible against the inventory list.

features.title: Flexible durations
features.text: From a couple of weeks between leases to year-long postings, billed per month on measured volume — in writing, in advance.

features.title: Optional insurance during storage
features.text: Storage-period cover is available and explained separately from transit cover — different risk, different policy, both documented.

faqs.q: How does household storage actually work?
faqs.a: We pack and collect like a normal move, inventory every box, seal and store your goods, then re-deliver when you call. You can retrieve specific boxes mid-term against the inventory list.

Perishables, liquids that can leak, flammables, documents of title, cash/jewellery and anything illegal. Clothes, books, furniture, appliances and kitchenware are the standard profile — we'll flag edge cases at survey.
By measured volume per month, stated in writing before pickup. There are no hidden 'handling' discoveries later — in/out handling and monthly storage are separate, named lines you approve first.

faqs.q: Is my stuff insured while in storage?
faqs.a: Storage cover is distinct from transit insurance and is offered as an option with written terms — scope, exclusions and claims process documented before you sign.
